finding.claim: SafeListSanitizer keeps one PermitScrubber per sanitizer instance and rewrites its tags/attributes allowlist on every call. If one instance is shared across threads and two calls pass different tags:/attributes: options, a call can be scrubbed with another call's allowlist. This is a low-severity, conditional issue: it needs a shared instance and per-call allowlists that differ in privilege.
finding.source: Per-call options[:tags] / options[:attributes] (scrubbers.rb:164-166), which a caller may derive from per-user or per-role data. Also the instance itself, if memoized or held in a constant, as the README examples suggest.
finding.sink: fragment.scrub!(@permit_scrubber) at scrubbers.rb:167 runs with whatever @permit_scrubber.tags/attributes currently holds, which another thread may have overwritten after this call's assignment at lines 165-166.

trace.note: ComposedSanitize#sanitize entry point; options passed through unchanged

finding.guards_checked: Checked: validate! (scrubbers.rb:137-160) enforces Enumerable and strips mglyph/malignmark/noscript, but not the race. tags=/attributes= dup their input (scrubbers.rb:59, 63), so caller mutation can't leak in, but there is still no synchronization on the shared instance. Class-level defaults are dup'd per class (scrubbers.rb:152-153). Loofah's bottom-up traversal ignores scrub return values (loofah/scrubber.rb:125-129), so the STOP returns don't skip siblings. The race itself is unguarded. Exploitability depends on the caller sharing an instance and varying options by privilege; with only the default allowlists it is not exploitable.
